title: Add plan re-confirmation step on plan changes in ticket-do
story: As a developer, I want the agent to re-confirm the updated plan with me whenever the plan changes mid-execution, so that I always have visibility and approval before implementation continues.
acceptance_criteria: ticket-do instructs the agent to re-present the full updated plan whenever a change is made mid-execution
The agent waits for explicit user confirmation before continuing after a plan change
The re-confirmation step is identical in form to the initial plan confirmation step

title: Replace LLM-driven verbatim field entry in ticket-do with explicit instruction
story: As a developer, I want verbatim text I provide to be placed into ticket fields exactly as given, without the agent interpreting or acting on it, so that data entry is reliable.
acceptance_criteria: ticket-do explicitly instructs the agent to treat user-provided verbatim text as inert data to be transcribed, not as instructions to act on
The agent asks for confirmation before taking any action when the user is in the middle of providing field values
The ticket field contains the exact text the user provided, with no modifications, interpretations, or additions by the agent.

title: Local script to retrieve next ticket number
story: As a developer, I want a local script that retrieves the next ticket number so that I don't contribute towards LLM API usage limits.

title: Script to record user retro feedback verbatim
story: As a developer, I want a script to record my retro feedback directly into the ticket JSON so that the LLM cannot interpret or act on it.
acceptance_criteria: A script exists that accepts a ticket ID and prompts for user_retro text via stdin
The script writes the input verbatim to the user_retro field of the matching ticket in current-sprint.json
The retro command instructs the agent to invoke this script for collecting user_retro rather than asking in chat

title: Django project scaffolding with custom user model
story: As a developer, I want a Django project set up with a custom user model so that I have a solid foundation for the backend with room for future user model extensions.
acceptance_criteria: Django project exists at backend/ in the monorepo root
Custom user model (CustomUser) extends AbstractUser
AUTH_USER_MODEL is set to the custom user model
Initial migrations are created and apply cleanly
Django admin has a `CustomUserAdmin` class registered for `CustomUser`
The default Django welcome page loads without error when running `python manage.py runserver`
A `requirements.txt` exists at `backend/` with Django pinned
A virtual environment exists at `backend/venv/`
A test exists verifying that a `CustomUser` instance can be saved to and retrieved from the database
non_goals: Database configuration (covered in a separate ticket)
Docker container for the Django app
assumptions: SQLite is used as the default database for this ticket; Postgres configuration is covered in ticket 054

user: we should be checking at some stage (ticket-do or retro) to see if there are any things that should be added to the readme

title: Refactor Exercise component: extract state hook and phase subcomponents
story: As a developer, I want the Exercise component split so that state logic and rendering are independently testable
acceptance_criteria: All exercise state (phase, word, text, annotations, apiKey, durationSeconds, isValidating, apiKeyError) is extracted into a custom hook with its own test file using renderHook
Each phase (idle, writing, results) is rendered by a separate component that accepts state and callbacks as props
Each phase component has its own test file exercising it independently via props
Each phase component has a Storybook story covering at least its default state
The Exercise component calls the hook and delegates rendering to the phase components
All existing Exercise tests continue to pass
non_goals: Adding new features or fixing bugs beyond those directly enabled by the refactor
Migrating to a different state management approach (e.g., context, Zustand)
assumptions: Storybook is already installed and configured in the project
The current Exercise component has existing tests worth preserving

title: Add ability to add tickets to an in-progress sprint
story: As a developer, I want to be able to move groomed tickets into the current sprint so that I can start work on them before closing the sprint.
acceptance_criteria: Given a ticket ID, the skill moves the ticket from backlog.json into current-sprint.json
If the specified ticket has not been groomed (groomed_at is null), the skill exits with an error and does not move the ticket
If the specified ticket is not found in the backlog, the skill exits with an error
non_goals: Reordering or prioritizing tickets within the sprint
Moving tickets out of the sprint back to the backlog
assumptions: current-sprint.json and backlog.json exist and follow the established schema
Tickets have a groomed_at field that is non-null when groomed (the schema is stable)
The skill is invoked with a single ticket ID argument

title: Postgres Docker container and Django DB connection
story: As a developer, I want a Dockerized Postgres instance with Django connected to it so that I can persist data without installing Postgres locally.
acceptance_criteria: docker-compose.yml at repo root defines a Postgres service
Django DATABASES setting connects to the containerized Postgres via env vars
python manage.py migrate runs successfully against the containerized DB
DB credentials are configured via a .env file (not hardcoded)
.env.example documents all required variables
non_goals: Database backup or volume persistence configuration
Multi-service orchestration beyond the single Postgres container
assumptions: Docker and Docker Compose are installed locally
Docker Compose v2 syntax is used (not legacy v1)
